summary: As of Friday, September 25, before the U.S. open, the Nasdaq setup remains slightly negative, with the dominant pressure still coming from very high Treasury yields and elevated energy prices. Thursday's session was pressured by the same mix: technology shares were among the weakest groups as Brent briefly reached about $107, while the 10-year Treasury yield ended around 5.20%. The Nasdaq Composite closed at 26,939.37, nearly flat after recovering from a materially weaker open, showing that buyers are still willing to defend technology even as the discount-rate backdrop remains difficult. A reliable live Nasdaq-100 futures quote was not yet available in sources verified by 06:00 Turkey time, so this brief does not infer an overnight futures move.

The overnight balance is somewhat better than Thursday's worst case but still fragile. Oil eased modestly in Asian trading on reports of possible U.S.-Iran diplomatic progress, which is supportive if it persists because it could reduce pressure on inflation expectations and bond yields. Brent nevertheless remains around the mid-$100s and Middle East security risk is unresolved. The Trump-Xi summit produced no major breakthrough, limiting the immediate upside catalyst for China-sensitive technology and semiconductor shares. With the 10-year near multi-decade highs, today's durable-goods data, Michigan inflation expectations and Fed commentary can quickly change the rates narrative.

events.title: 1. Durable goods orders — 8:30 ET
events.detail: August durable-goods orders and the ex-transportation measure are the first major U.S. macro test. The Nasdaq reaction is likely to run mainly through Treasury yields: unusually strong demand could reinforce tighter-policy expectations, while a softer report could provide relief to long-duration technology valuations.

events.title: 2. New York Fed President John Williams — 5:15 ET
events.detail: Williams participates in a monetary-policy panel in Oxford with moderated Q&A expected. With the 10-year yield around 5.2% and expectations for further Fed tightening elevated, comments on inflation, policy restrictiveness or the rate path can matter before the U.S. data releases.

events.title: 3. University of Michigan sentiment and inflation expectations — 10:00 ET
events.detail: The final September consumer-sentiment reading arrives with one-year and five-year inflation expectations. The preliminary survey showed very weak sentiment and elevated inflation expectations, making the inflation components especially important for Treasuries and technology multiples.

events.title: 4. U.S.-Iran / Middle East and oil headlines — ongoing
events.detail: Oil eased early Friday as markets weighed a possible diplomatic path toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz, but regional security risks remain acute. Credible de-escalation could become today's strongest unscheduled upside catalyst for Nasdaq through lower oil and yields; renewed escalation could quickly reverse that.

events.title: 5. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack — 2:00 ET
events.detail: Hammack participates in an inflation-policy panel in Cleveland. Her appearance comes after the market has absorbed durable goods and Michigan data, so it can reinforce or challenge the day's developing rates narrative.

watchIntoOpen: What I’d watch into the open: the cleanest constructive scenario is oil continuing to retreat while the 10-year yield stabilizes or falls, with durable goods and Michigan inflation expectations doing nothing to revive the tightening narrative; that would give semiconductors and mega-cap technology room to reassert leadership. The downside scenario is resilient macro data or hawkish Fed commentary pushing yields above Thursday's already elevated levels while Middle East headlines send crude back toward recent highs. With the Trump-Xi meeting delivering no obvious breakthrough, rates, oil and semiconductor participation should be the best tells on whether Thursday's late resilience can carry into Friday.
keyTimes: The U.S. cash market opens at 9:30 ET, which is 16:30 in Istanbul. Key windows are 5:15 ET (12:15 Istanbul) for New York Fed President Williams, 8:30 ET (15:30 Istanbul) for durable goods, 10:00 ET (17:00 Istanbul) for final Michigan sentiment and inflation expectations, and 2:00 ET (21:00 Istanbul) for Cleveland Fed President Hammack. Middle East and oil headlines remain unscheduled intraday catalysts.
